summary: Thousand Oaks sprawls across 55 square miles of the Conejo Valley — one of the largest cities by area in Ventura County — yet nearly half that footprint is preserved open space, with over 15,000 acres of trails threading through the Santa Monica Mountains and Conejo Valley foothills that ring the city on three sides. That geography creates a striking daily rhythm: suburban shopping plazas and office parks sit minutes from ridgeline hikes with Pacific views, and the Amgen campus — one of the world's largest biotech headquarters — anchors a healthcare and life-sciences employment cluster that means a meaningful share of jobs are local rather than requiring the notorious US-101 crawl to Los Angeles. Still, the home-price-to-income ratio tells a tighter story than the $134K median household income might suggest: at a median home value above $951K, that's roughly a 7:1 ratio, and median rent of $2,580 absorbs a substantial monthly share even at that income level. The 75°F average daily high and nearly 10 hours of sunshine year-round deliver reliably mild weather with almost no humidity, though summer days in the interior valley push well past that average. With a total crime rate around 1,222 per 100K — notably low property and violent crime for a city this size — and a property-crime profile dominated by larceny rather than burglary or vehicle theft, the infrastructure reflects a car-dependent, spread-out suburb more than a walkable town center. Thousand Oaks is essentially a well-maintained, trail-laced valley where biotech paychecks compete with Southern California land costs, and the tradeoff for all that open sky is that almost everything requires a windshield.
